claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength in its simple solid-solution state.
Deformation of single-phase CoCrFeNiTi is dominated by easy dislocation glide.
Homogeneous single-phase CoCrFeNiTi lacks nano-precipitates, deformation twins, and other secondary structural obstacles.
Nano-precipitates and dislocation networks impede dislocation motion and can increase strength.
Deformation twins act as barriers that increase hardness and strength.
AlCrCuFeNiTi and CuFeNiMnTi have higher hardness and compressive strength because their compositions promote nanoscale secondary phases or dislocation networks.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi material is an as-cast, homogeneous, single-phase solid solution with minimal nano-precipitate and twin-boundary content.
Controlled aging can induce nanoscale precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
Controlled aging can promote twin formation in CoCrFeNiTi.
A uniform simple solid solution permits dislocations to move with little resistance.
Low resistance to dislocation motion gives CoCrFeNiTi good plasticity and machinability at the cost of hardness and strength.
Introducing nanoscale precipitates or similar barriers will increase the hardness and compressive strength of CoCrFeNiTi.
An aged CoCrFeNiTi alloy that develops nanoscale precipitates or twins will be harder and have greater compressive strength than the as-cast alloy.
The strengthening produced by aging will reduce plastic strain to failure.
The proposed mechanism applies to CoCrFeNiTi between 25 °C and 600 °C under compression and hardness-testing conditions.
In additively manufactured equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, fine grains, high dislocation density, and fine precipitates contribute to excellent mechanical properties from 25 °C to 600 °C.
Slip and deformation twinning are active deformation mechanisms from 25 °C to 600 °C in additively manufactured equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.

contradictions.description: The boundary says the hypothesis applies to CoCrFeNiTi processed to retain a single-phase structure, whereas the intervention is intended to create secondary precipitates, which would make the treated state multiphase unless the stated boundary refers only to the starting state.
